name: Zilebesiran
summary: Zilebesiran is Alnylam's subcutaneous GalNAc-siRNA against liver angiotensinogen, dosed 300 mg every six months and co-developed with Roche. The Phase 3 is ZENITH (NCT07181109), an event-driven cardiovascular outcomes Phase 3 of about 11,000 patients against placebo. It enrols uncontrolled hypertension (office SBP 140-170) on 2-4 antihypertensives including a diuretic, with established CVD or high CV risk. The primary endpoint is time to CV death, MI, stroke or HF event, and primary completion is estimated for 2030-09-23. Price anchor: Baxfendy (baxdrostat), the branded add-on approved in 2026 for hypertension not adequately controlled on other agents, at a WAC of $900 per 30 tablets ($10,950 a year), less the 52.7% by which Entresto's Medicare negotiated price sits below its CMS gross. Uptake anchor: Leqvio, the twice-yearly siRNA in CV prevention, reached 50,979 Medicare beneficiaries in its third full year, 0.44% of the 11.5mm US adults with ASCVD recommended add-on therapy. The engine needs a 0.0177 peak to match that. Alnylam keeps 50% of US profit and receives tiered low double-digit royalties from Roche outside the US (10-Q 0001178670-26-000062).

therapy_mode.source: ZENITH design: zilebesiran 300 mg every six months against placebo, open-ended until the event-driven CV outcomes analysis (Alnylam 8-K exhibit 99.1, 2025-10-30, 0001628280-25-047342; clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07181109)
therapy_mode.note: Continuous maintenance dosing, one injection every six months
therapy_mode.check: 8-K exhibit 99.1 of 2025-10-30 (0001628280-25-047342, book filing_sections): ZENITH evaluates 'zilebesiran (300 mg) administered every six months compared to placebo'. Continuous twice-yearly maintenance dosing is chronic. Book trials table: NCT07181109, Phase 3, recruiting, 11,000, primary outcome time to CV death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke or HF event.

list_price_per_patient.source: Baxfendy (baxdrostat, AstraZeneca) WAC of $900 per 30 tablets, once daily: $30 a day x 365 = $10,950 a year. $10,950 is the annual WAC ICER's August 2026 hypertension draft evidence report used for baxdrostat, with an identical placeholder for lorundrostat (AJMC, 'ICER Draft Flags High Cost of New Hypertension Drug Class', ajmc.com/view/icer-draft-flags-high-cost-of-new-hypertension-drug-class). Fierce Pharma ('AZ's blood pressure newcomer Baxfendy fails to meet cost-effectiveness bar, ICER says') reports the same $900 per 30 tablets annualised as twelve fills, $10,800
list_price_per_patient.note: Judgement on the comparator. The brief says a published annual list price beats the CMS convention, and Baxfendy is the closest marketed product in the same disease and setting. Its label (DailyMed, in the book's labels table, effective 2026-09-18) covers hypertension in adults not adequately controlled on other agents, and the book's Hypertension pool was drawn for it. It has no CMS demand row yet. Cross-check: Leqvio, the same-modality twice-yearly siRNA, reads $6,135 per CMS Part B beneficiary in 2024 (lookup.py demand Leqvio: $296,288,761 over 48,298). Less the 6% Part B add-on, that is a net $5,788, close to the $5,184 net here. Case for higher: if ZENITH succeeds, zilebesiran carries an outcomes claim that Baxfendy's label says it lacks ('There are no controlled trials demonstrating risk reduction'). Case for lower: ICER found the aldosterone synthase inhibitors far above its value benchmarks at this price, which signals payer resistance to branded antihypertensives against generics. Discrepancy to flag: the book's baxdrostat seed prices Baxfendy off Leqvio's Part D $5,364, but Leqvio's Medicare beneficiaries sit 95% in Part B, and Baxfendy now has its own WAC
list_price_per_patient.check: Value unchanged; source wording corrected. Search: Fierce Pharma and pharmaphorum report ICER's WAC of $900 per 30 Baxfendy tablets and 'an annual cost before discounts and rebates of $10,800' (12 fills); AJMC reports ICER used a WAC of $10,950 a year. The researcher credited $10,950 to both outlets. 365 x $30 = $10,950 is the patient-year basis for a once-daily tablet, so 0.01095 stands. The report date 2026-08-12 was not seen; the searches show August 2026. Label checked in the book's labels table (DailyMed, Sep 18, 2026): 'in combination with other antihypertensive drugs ... in adults who are not adequately controlled on other agents' and 'There are no controlled trials demonstrating risk reduction of these events with BAXFENDY'. No Baxfendy row in drug_demand. Leqvio cross-check recomputed: Part B 2024 $296,288,761 / 48,298 = $6,135, x (1 - 0.056604) = $5,788; Part B share of Medicare beneficiaries 48,298 / 50,979 = 94.7%. The baxdrostat seed does carry Leqvio's Part D $5,364 (azn_baxfendy.csv). Judgement on the comparator is labelled with its case against; the Part B point (zilebesiran is likely HCP-administered like Leqvio) is the main one.

gross_to_net_pct.source: Measured on Entresto, the book's closest cardiovascular oral brand with a CMS negotiated price. CMS Part D 2024 gross: $4,020,321,686 over 364,166,283 tablets = $11.0398 a tablet (lookup.py demand Entresto). The Maximum Fair Price for 2026 is $5.2266 a tablet, NDC 00078-0659 (book negotiated_prices, cms_mfp; $295 per 30-day equivalent supply). 1 - 5.2266 / 11.0398 = 0.5266
gross_to_net_pct.note: Judgement. A WAC anchor takes neither house convention, so the discount is sourced. Direction checked: 0.527 comes off list, and net is $5,184 a patient-year. Case for a smaller discount: a Maximum Fair Price is negotiated for a drug seven or more years past launch, so it sits below what a new launch realises (backend/gross_to_net.py says so). If zilebesiran is buy-and-bill under Part B, as Leqvio is, only the 6% add-on comes off an ASP that is already net. Case for a larger one: the gross figure is 2024 and the MFP is 2026, so list-price growth in between understates the discount slightly, and primary-care hypertension is a heavily rebated generic-dominated class. The house 0.5 on a CMS Part D figure would give almost the same net
gross_to_net_pct.check: Recomputed from the book: Entresto Part D 2024 $4,020,321,686.4 / 364,166,283.49 units = $11.03977 a unit (lookup.py demand Entresto); negotiated_prices cms_mfp NDC 00078-0659, 2026: unit price $5.226585, $295.00 per 30-day equivalent supply. 1 - 5.226585 / 11.03977 = 0.52657. Direction right: share off list; net = $10,950 x 0.47343 = $5,184. A WAC anchor takes neither house convention and this discount is sourced and labelled a judgement with its case against (an MFP is a statutory price for a drug years past launch; under Part B only the 6% add-on would come off an ASP). The house 0.5 would give $5,475, within 6%.

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.source: Blais JE et al., 'Adherence to PCSK9 Inhibitors in Clinical Practice: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Observational Studies', JACC Adv 2026;5(5):102733, doi:10.1016/j.jacadv.2026.102733, PMID 42000553. Pooled 12-month discontinuation is 12.1% (95% CI 7.4-19.0) across alirocumab, evolocumab and inclisiran; 12-month persistence is 81.8%
discontinuation_pct.note: Judgement on the analogue: an injectable CV-prevention agent added to cheap orals, closest to zilebesiran's infrequent dosing. It is the same value the book's olpasiran and lepodisiran seeds carry. Those seeds call it an inclisiran figure, but the pooled studies are mostly alirocumab and evolocumab, and the paper notes limited inclisiran evidence. Case for higher: 1 minus the 81.8% persistence gives 0.182, and the paper finds persistence declining beyond 12 months. Hypertension is asymptomatic, and oral antihypertensive persistence is worse. Case for lower: an HCP-administered injection twice a year needs two visits a year. Discrepancy to flag: the baxdrostat seed's discontinuation source is text about advanced solid tumours
discontinuation_pct.check: PubMed PMID 42000553 (Blais JE et al., JACC Adv 2026;5(5):102733, doi:10.1016/j.jacadv.2026.102733): 12-month discontinuation 12.1% (95% CI 7.4-19.0), persistence 81.8%, 56 studies 'primarily evaluating alirocumab and evolocumab', limited evidence 'for inclisiran'. Olpasiran and lepodisiran seeds carry 0.121 (lookup.py seed). Judgement on the analogue, labelled with its case against.

forecast_start_year.source: NCT07181109 primary completion 2030-09-23, estimated (context file; book trials table, last update 2026-09-18)
forecast_start_year.note: Judgement on the timeline. Topline around late 2030, an NDA in 2031 and a standard review put launch around late 2031 or early 2032, so 2032 is the first full year. This is the same two-calendar-years-after-PCD rule the verified vepugratinib (PCD 2029-10 to 2031) and duvakitug (2028-09 to 2030) seeds use. Case for later: ZENITH is event-driven, so the PCD can slip with the event rate. Alnylam states a launch year for nucresiran ('by 2030', 10-Q 0001178670-26-000062) but none for zilebesiran. No BP-lowering filing ahead of the CVOT has been announced
forecast_start_year.check: Book trials table: NCT07181109 primary completion 2030-09-23 (estimated), last update 2026-09-18, start 2025-09-22. PCD plus two calendar years matches the verified vepugratinib (2029-10 to 2031) and duvakitug (2028-09 to 2030) seeds. Q2 2026 10-Q MD&A (0001178670-26-000062) states 'we continue to expect to launch nucresiran in ATTR-CM by 2030' and gives no zilebesiran launch year. An NME filed in 2031 on a 12-month standard review could make 2032 a part year; labelled a judgement.

exus_multiple.source: Leqvio FY2025: rest of world $623mm against US $575mm (Novartis annual report table, 0001114448-26-000004, in the book's asset_revenue_regions). 623 / 575 = 1.0835
exus_multiple.note: Judgement on the comparator. Leqvio is the twice-yearly siRNA in CV prevention, discovered by Alnylam and sold by one large partner worldwide, as zilebesiran will be with Roche outside the US. Case for lower: Repatha reads 1,353 / 1,663 = 0.814 (Amgen FY2025, sec_fsds, book), and Leqvio's ex-US share is lifted by a UK population-level agreement. Case for higher: Entresto reads 4,463 / 3,285 = 1.359 (same Novartis table). Roche books the ex-US sales. Alnylam's share of them is the royalty in economics_share, not this field
exus_multiple.check: Book asset_revenue_regions, Novartis annual report table 0001114448-26-000004: Leqvio FY2025 US $575mm, rest of world $623mm, 623 / 575 = 1.08348. Repatha FY2025 (10-K 0000318154-26-000010, sec_fsds) 1,353 / 1,663 = 0.814; Entresto 4,463 / 3,285 = 1.359. Leqvio 2024 to 2025 worldwide $754mm to $1,198mm (+58.9%). The UK population-level agreement in the case against was not checked.

economics_share.source: Alnylam 10-Q for the quarter to 2026-06-30 (0001178670-26-000062, filed 2026-07-30), MD&A 'Strategic Collaborations', repeated in the Q1 2026 10-Q (0001628280-26-028605): Roche holds co-exclusive rights to develop worldwide and commercialise in the U.S. and exclusive rights outside the U.S. 'We and Roche will share equally (50/50) profits and losses (including commercialization costs) of zilebesiran in the U.S.' Roche 'will pay us tiered, low double digit royalties based on net sales of zilebesiran on a country-by-country basis outside of the U.S.' Development costs are 40% Alnylam and 60% Roche. Alnylam FY2025 cost lines (10-K 0001628280-26-007497, book financials, edgar_companyfacts): revenue $3,713.9mm, cost of revenue $677.2mm (0.182331), SG&A $1,210.7mm (0.325992), R&D $1,319.8mm (0.355357)
economics_share.note: Judgement, and provisional. A blend weighted by the ex-US multiple: US 0.5 as a 50/50 profit share; ex-US a royalty Alnylam RECEIVES, netted as royalty / margin. The margin is 1 - 0.182331 - 0.325992 - 0.355357 = 0.13632, with other_costs_pct left out because ALNY has no company rows yet (the NBIX osavampator precedent). 'Low double digit' is taken at its 10% floor, as the votoplam seed does, so ex-US is 0.10 / 0.13632 = 0.7336. (0.5 + 1.0835 x 0.7336) / 2.0835 = 0.6215. Recompute once ALNY's company rows land: at a 0.20 margin the share is 0.500, and at the ~30% non-GAAP operating margin Alnylam targets through 2030 (FY2025 10-K MD&A) it is 0.413. At a 12% royalty it is 0.698, and at 15% (ex-US capped at 1.0) 0.760. Not in this field: up to $2.15bn of further Roche milestones receivable; $243mm Alnylam owes Blackstone in 16 quarterly payments on approval, a fixed payment not a royalty (10-Q note 9); and the 40/60 development cost split against a 50/50 US profit split
economics_share.check: Terms read in the book's filing_sections. Q2 2026 10-Q MD&A (0001178670-26-000062, filed 2026-07-30), and the same paragraph in the Q1 10-Q (0001628280-26-028605): Roche has co-exclusive rights to develop worldwide and commercialise in the U.S. and exclusive rights outside it; 'We and Roche will share equally (50/50) profits and losses (including commercialization costs) of zilebesiran in the U.S.'; Roche 'will pay us tiered, low double digit royalties based on net sales of zilebesiran on a country-by-country basis outside of the U.S.'; development costs 40% Alnylam, 60% Roche; up to $2.15bn more in development, regulatory and sales milestones. 10-Q notes: $243.0mm to Blackstone 'in 16 equal quarterly payments over four years triggered upon regulatory approval of zilebesiran in specified countries'. CONFIRMED FOR RE-STRIKE: US profit share 0.5; ex-US royalty received, 'tiered, low double digit', no rate disclosed, taken at the 10% floor (votoplam precedent). Cost lines checked in book financials and the FY2025 10-K MD&A table: revenue $3,713,937k; COGS $677,166k (0.182331); SG&A $1,210,713k (0.325992); R&D $1,319,775k (0.355357); margin 0.136320. (0.5 + 1.0835 x 0.10 / 0.136320) / 2.0835 = 0.62147. Re-strike as (0.5 + 1.0835 x 0.10 / m) / 2.0835 with m = 1 - cogs - sga - rd - other_costs from ALNY's final block. Sensitivities recomputed: m 0.20 -> 0.500; m 0.30 -> 0.413; 12% royalty -> 0.698; 15% capped at 1.0 ex-US -> 0.760 (uncapped 0.812; the cap is a choice, not arithmetic, since a royalty carries none of the costs). Notes: the block leaves out 'cost of collaborations and royalties' ($4,705k, 0.13% of revenue; reported operating margin 13.51% gives 0.625); Alnylam's COGS carries Sanofi's Amvuttra royalty, which depresses m and lifts the ex-US term. The ~30% non-GAAP operating margin through 2030 is in the FY2025 10-K MD&A.

prevalence.source: carried by the book: baxdrostat seed, 14,640,000 ('roughly 122mm US adults have hypertension (American Heart Association 2025 statistics), of whom about 12% are uncontrolled on multiple agents')
prevalence.note: Carried by the book. The book's Hypertension pool is the resistant population (uncontrolled on three or more agents) drawn for baxdrostat, and one figure per disease is the rule. It is not ZENITH's label population, which is uncontrolled hypertension on two or more antihypertensives, one a diuretic, with established CVD or high CV risk: wider on drug count, narrower on risk. eligible_pct carries both differences. The book's 'Cardiovascular Diseases' pool (53.4mm, elevated Lp(a), olpasiran and pelacarsen seeds) is not this label's and is not modelled. ZENITH is one trial, and the CV outcomes it tests are a claim within the hypertension label
prevalence.check: Value stays null (carried). Note corrected only: it called the resistant pool 'the pool the label reaches'. lookup.py pool Hypertension: 14,640,000 (baxdrostat seed, 12% of ~122mm) is the only Hypertension prevalence in the book. ZENITH population per Alnylam 8-K exhibit 99.1 (2025-10-30) and Q2 2026 10-Q: 'uncontrolled hypertension on two or more antihypertensives, one being a diuretic', 'with either established CV disease or at high risk for CV disease'. Book-level flag, not changed here: 14.64mm is above every NHANES aTRH count I saw, 10.3mm (Carey 2019, 2018 definition), 7.6mm (Kaczmarski 2019), 6.99mm (Earle 2026).

incidence.source: carried by the book: baxdrostat seed, 1,200,000 ('about 1% of the treated hypertensive population becomes resistant each year')
incidence.note: Carried by the book. The engine carries every untreated patient forward (carryover 1.0), so the untreated pool grows by the full inflow each year. A stable pool would need about 1,200,000 / 14,640,000 = 8.2% to leave each year (carryover about 0.918). Not set here, because the penetration below is calibrated on the default
incidence.check: Book carries 1,200,000 for Hypertension (baxdrostat seed); null is right. The engine scales it by eligible_pct and the ex-US multiple (forecast.patients_for_indication). Assembly item: the house rule holds a chronic pool stationary at retention = pool / (pool + inflow) = 14.64 / 15.84 = 0.924242 (the note's 0.918 is 1 - inflow/pool, a different formula). With carryover 1.0 the eligible untreated pool roughly doubles over 20 years. If untreated_carryover_pct 0.924242 is added, penetration re-solves to 0.019624 on the same Leqvio target (engine run), and US treated stock at the corrected eligible share falls from 0.62mm to 0.39mm in year 14.

eligible_pct.source: Three NHANES papers. (1) Uncontrolled at 140/90, ZENITH's floor: of US adults on antihypertensives, 5.7% take three classes and 2.8% four or more with BP at or above 140/90, against 19.7% with aTRH by the 2018 AHA definition. 8.5 / 19.7 = 0.431472 of the resistant pool (Carey RM et al., Hypertension 2019;73:424-431, doi:10.1161/HYPERTENSIONAHA.118.12191, PMID 30580690). (2) Two-drug patients, whom ZENITH enrols and the resistant pool excludes: of treated US adults with BP at or above 140/90 in 2013-2016, 40.2% take one class and 35.1% two, so 24.7% take three or more; two-drug patients are 35.1 / 24.7 = 1.421053 times the three-plus group (Derington CG et al., Hypertension 2020;75:973-981, doi:10.1161/HYPERTENSIONAHA.119.14360, PMID 32148129). (3) Established CVD (prior MI, HF or stroke): 36.4% of uncontrolled aTRH, and 15.9% of adults controlled on fewer than three drugs (Kaczmarski KR et al., BMC Nephrol 2019;20:138, doi:10.1186/s12882-019-1315-0, PMID 31023262). 0.431472 x 0.364 = 0.157056 on three or more drugs; 0.431472 x 1.421053 x 0.159 = 0.097490 on two; total 0.254546
eligible_pct.note: Judgement: a sourced floor for ZENITH's label, uncontrolled hypertension on two or more antihypertensives (one a diuretic) with established CVD or high CV risk. The book's pool is the resistant population, so eligible_pct carries the two-drug patients the trial enrols (0.613 of the pool before the CVD filter) and the CVD filter the pool lacks. Applied to the book's pool: 3.73mm US patients. Floor on two counts: the two-drug group takes the 15.9% CVD share Kaczmarski measured in adults controlled on one or two drugs, where uncontrolled two-drug patients likely carry more; and the trial's high-CV-risk arm without established CVD is not counted, because no US share for it was found. Ceiling if every uncontrolled patient on two or more drugs qualified: 0.431 + 0.613 = 1.045. Kaczmarski's CVD definition leaves out angina, revascularisation and PAD. Case for lower: ZENITH requires a diuretic (86.8% of aTRH take one, Kaczmarski; the share among two-drug patients is not given, though ACE inhibitor or ARB plus diuretic is the commonest dual regimen, Derington), excludes five or more drugs (8.49% of aTRH, Earle WB et al., Hypertension 2026, PMID 41778325), and NHANES single-visit BP counts white-coat and non-adherent patients. Derington groups diuretics as one class and Carey does not, so the 1.42 ratio is taken within Derington; Derington's own three-plus share (31.0% x 24.7% = 7.7% of treated) sits near Carey's 8.5%
eligible_pct.check: 0.157056 -> 0.254546. Inputs confirmed in PMC full texts: Carey (PMC6693520) 5.7%, 2.8%, 19.7%, 10.3mm; Kaczmarski (PMC6485047) 36.4% prior CVD in uncontrolled aTRH, 48.5% controlled aTRH, 31.4% controlled on 3 drugs, 15.9% controlled on fewer than 3, 86.8% diuretic, 5.33 of 7.6mm uncontrolled; Earle (PMC13488949) 8.49% on five or more. The researcher's floor dropped the two-drug patients ZENITH enrols ('two or more antihypertensives, one being a diuretic': 8-K 0001628280-25-047342 and Q2 2026 10-Q) because the book's pool excludes them, but eligible_pct is the place to carry a label that reaches past the pool. Derington (PMC7398637): among treated adults at or above 140/90, 40.2% on one class and 35.1% on two (2013-2016). Adding them at the lowest measured CVD share gives 0.097490. Alternative arithmetic on Derington's own shares, 31.0% x 35.1% / 19.7% x 0.159 = 0.0878, gives 0.2449; within 4%. The 'aged 55+, 10-year ASCVD risk above 15%' criterion in the researcher's note could not be checked (Amass quota exhausted, ClinicalTrials.gov blocked) and is not used.

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of the eligible untreated pool per year
penetration_peak_pct.source: Solved in the engine (forecast.derive_new_patients and treated_stock, with the ramp and discontinuation here) to reproduce Leqvio's measured capture at the same age. Leqvio had 50,979 Medicare beneficiaries in 2024, its third full year after approval in December 2021: Part B 48,298 plus Part D 2,681 (lookup.py demand Leqvio). Its pool is the 18.7mm US adults with ASCVD, of whom 61.4% are recommended add-on lipid-lowering therapy = 11.48mm (Alanaeme CJ et al., Am Heart J Plus 2022;21:100201, doi:10.1016/j.ahjo.2022.100201, PMID 37168932). Share 0.444%. The engine reaches it at year index 2 with a peak of 0.01768
penetration_peak_pct.note: Judgement: the multiple is 1.0, so zilebesiran takes its eligible pool at the pace Leqvio took its own. Cross-check: Leqvio's all-payer US revenue of $575mm in 2025 (index 3), at the Part B net of $5,788 a beneficiary, is about 99,300 patient-years, or 0.865% of the pool. The engine needs 0.01727 to match that, so the two measures agree. The Medicare count can double-count patients in both Parts, and it leaves out non-Medicare patients. Case for higher: zilebesiran would launch with outcomes data, which Leqvio lacked (ORION-4 pending), with twice-yearly dosing aimed at hypertension non-adherence, and with Roche's scale. Case for lower: oral aldosterone synthase inhibitors (Baxfendy launched 2026; lorundrostat) arrive years earlier and cheaper. Hypertension is run in primary care, where in-office injectables are less established than in lipid clinics. ICER's finding on the ASIs signals payer friction. On this peak and the corrected eligible share (0.254546, 3.73mm US), the US treated stock reaches about 0.29mm by year 9 and 0.62mm by year 14 at the engine's default carryover (engine run). Held stationary (carryover 0.924242) the peak re-solves to 0.019624 and the stock is 0.22mm and 0.39mm. Re-solved to 0.019624 on the same Leqvio target (0.44% of the pool on therapy in its third full year) once the stationary carryover is set, per the second reader's engine run; it was 0.017679 on an unbounded pool
penetration_peak_pct.check: Value 0.017679 confirmed; note corrected only (its treated-stock figures were for the old eligible share). Recomputed with forecast.derive_new_patients and treated_stock (k 0.657, midpoint 5, discontinuation 0.121, inflow/pool 1.2/14.64): Leqvio 2024 Medicare 48,298 (Part B) + 2,681 (Part D) = 50,979 over 18.7mm x 61.4% = 11.48mm = 0.4440% (Alanaeme, PMID 37168932, abstract confirmed) is reached at index 2 with peak 0.017679. Revenue cross-check: $575mm / $5,788 = 99,355 patient-years = 0.865% at index 3 -> 0.017271. With no inflow the Medicare target needs 0.021238. At the old eligible share the engine gives 0.18mm (y9) and 0.38mm (y14), matching the researcher. Multiple 1.0 over Leqvio is labelled a judgement with its case against. Leqvio approved December 2021, so 2024 is index 2. | Assembler: 0.017679 -> 0.019624, the second reader's re-solve with carryover 0.924242

ramp_steepness.source: Reused from the baxdrostat seed (same pool) and the olpasiran and lepodisiran seeds: Leqvio's CMS Part D beneficiaries 721 (2022) to 2,681 (2024), k = ln(2,681/721)/2 = 0.657 (lookup.py demand Leqvio). Leqvio Part B 2023-2024 growth corroborates it: ln(48,298/24,690) = 0.671
ramp_steepness.note: Judgement: a measured growth rate, not a full logistic fit. My three-point least-squares logistic on Leqvio's Medicare beneficiaries (7,500, 26,530, 50,979) gives k 1.67 with a plateau of 64,700. Leqvio's 59% revenue growth in 2025 ($754mm to $1,198mm, book asset_revenue) contradicts that plateau, so no reliable fit exists yet. Discrepancy to flag: the baxdrostat seed's source text cites Enhertu's fit (k 1.08, midpoint 2.2) against the values 0.657 and 5.0 it actually carries
ramp_steepness.check: lookup.py demand Leqvio: Part D 721 (2022) to 2,681 (2024), ln(2,681/721)/2 = 0.6567; Part B ln(48,298/24,690) = 0.6710. Olpasiran, lepodisiran and baxdrostat seeds carry 0.657; the baxdrostat seed's source text cites Enhertu's k 1.08 and midpoint 2.2 against the 0.657 and 5 it carries, as flagged. The three-point logistic through 7,500, 26,530 and 50,979 is exact at k 1.666 and plateau 64,924 (the note's 64,700 is close, not exact); Leqvio's 2025 revenue +58.9% contradicts that plateau, as the note says.

ramp_midpoint_year.source: Reused from the baxdrostat, olpasiran and lepodisiran seeds (Leqvio as the analogue: 'Cardiovascular prevention is adopted slowly')
ramp_midpoint_year.note: Judgement, not fitted. Leqvio was still growing 59% in its fourth full year, which is consistent with a midpoint several years out. Penetration_peak_pct is calibrated on this curve, so moving the midpoint means re-solving the peak

untreated_carryover_pct.unit: share of the untreated pool retained per year
untreated_carryover_pct.source: derived to hold the book's resistant-hypertension pool at its measured size, the method the remternetug and direclidine seeds use: the pool (14,640,000, the baxdrostat seed's) and its inflow (1,200,000 a year, the same seed's) are stationary only if exits equal entries, which sets retention at 14.64 / (14.64 + 1.20) = 0.924242
untreated_carryover_pct.note: JUDGEMENT, the second reader's recommendation: with no exit in the engine the eligible untreated pool roughly doubles over twenty years. The case against: resistant hypertension is chronic and exits are mostly deaths, slower than 7.6% a year
